findings.problem: WithUnifiedPagination is not used by any tool, only by pagination_test.go. It also copies the "page", "perPage" and "after" definitions that WithPagination and WithCursorPagination already have, so the same schema text exists in three places.
findings.fix: Delete WithUnifiedPagination and its test case. Then pull the parameter definitions into private options (pageOption, perPageOption, afterOption) and build WithPagination and WithCursorPagination from them.

findings.problem: PaginationParams gained an After field and a ToGraphQLParams method. No REST tool reads them, and the GraphQL tools use CursorPaginationParams instead. OptionalPaginationParams now also reads and type-checks "after" on every REST tool, so a REST tool can fail on a parameter its schema does not declare.
findings.fix: Remove After and PaginationParams.ToGraphQLParams. Remove the "after" lookup from OptionalPaginationParams so it only reads page and perPage. Keep cursor handling only in CursorPaginationParams/OptionalCursorPaginationParams, and drop the matching test cases.

findings.problem: OptionalPaginationParams hardcodes a default perPage of 30. The new DefaultGraphQLPageSize const (also 30) sits in graphql.go, so the package now keeps two separate sources for the same default.
findings.fix: Add one DefaultPageSize const in pagination.go and use it in both OptionalPaginationParams and OptionalCursorPaginationParams. Delete graphql.go, or keep in it only GraphQL-specific helpers (see the next finding).

findings.problem: discussionsPageInfo/toMap and discussionsPaginationVars are general GraphQL connection helpers, but they carry discussion names and live in discussions.go. graphql.go was added as the place for GraphQL helpers and holds only a const. The helper also goes through GraphQLPaginationParams (*int32/*string) only to turn the values straight back into githubv4 types.
findings.fix: Move them to graphql.go as graphQLPageInfo and cursorPaginationVars(request) (the latter could also be a method on CursorPaginationParams). Have them return githubv4.Int/*githubv4.String directly, and remove GraphQLPaginationParams if nothing else uses it.

findings.problem: The new list_sub_issues tool declares its own "page" and "per_page" parameters (no min/max) and reads them by hand. Every other paginated tool uses WithPagination() with "perPage", so this tool's schema and validation don't match the rest of the package.
findings.fix: Use WithPagination() in the tool definition and OptionalPaginationParams(request) in the handler. Rename per_page to perPage in sub_issue_test.go and update the toolsnap.

findings.problem: The new test helpers repeat helpers that already exist. subIssueClientFn is stubGetClientFromHTTPFn (server_test.go). subIssueHandler and subIssueQueryHandler are expectRequestBody/expectQueryParams(...).andThen(mockResponse(...)) (helper_test.go). callSubIssueTool hand-builds the request and text extraction that createMCPRequest/getTextResult/getErrorResult already do.
findings.fix: Replace subIssueClientFn with stubGetClientFromHTTPFn. Replace subIssueHandler/subIssueQueryHandler with expectRequestBody/expectQueryParams(t, ...).andThen(mockResponse(t, status, body)). In callSubIssueTool, use createMCPRequest and getTextResult/getErrorResult, or remove it.

findings.problem: ListCommits sets perPage to 30 when it is 0. That can never happen, because OptionalPaginationParams already defaults perPage to 30, so this is dead code that repeats the default.
findings.fix: Delete the perPage local and the if block, and use pagination.PerPage directly in CommitsListOptions.

findings.problem: ListIssues declares WithPagination() but reads "page" and "perPage" by type-asserting request.GetArguments(). It skips OptionalPaginationParams, so it gets no defaults and no type errors, unlike the other list tools.
findings.fix: Call pagination, err := OptionalPaginationParams(request), return a tool error if err is set, and set opts.ListOptions = github.ListOptions{Page: pagination.Page, PerPage: pagination.PerPage}.

findings.problem: The tail_lines default of 500 is written twice: in mcp.DefaultNumber(500) at line 562 and in the hand-written `if tailLines == 0 { tailLines = 500 }`.
findings.fix: Add a const defaultTailLines = 500, use it in mcp.DefaultNumber, and read the value with OptionalIntParamWithDefault(request, "tail_lines", defaultTailLines) instead of the manual zero check.

findings.problem: handleFailedJobLogs drops the json.Marshal error (`r, _ :=`), while every other path in the file handles it.
findings.fix: Return MarshalledTextResult(result), or check the error the same way the rest of the function does.

findings.problem: userOrOrgHandler fills TotalCount and IncompleteResults with GetTotal()/GetIncompleteResults(), then sets them again from the same pointers in two `if result.X != nil` blocks. The second step does nothing.
findings.fix: Delete the two `if result.Total != nil` / `if result.IncompleteResults != nil` blocks.

findings.problem: The comment says sort defaults to "created", but the code passes the user's sort value unchanged and sets no default. The comment is wrong.
findings.fix: Delete the comment, or set the default it describes if that behaviour is wanted.

kept.fix: Delete the perPage local and the if block, and use pagination.PerPage directly in CommitsListOptions.
kept.why: OptionalPaginationParams already defaults perPage to 30, so `if perPage == 0` in ListCommits can only be reached when a caller passes 0 explicitly. It repeats the default as dead code.

kept.problem: ListIssues declares WithPagination() but reads "page" and "perPage" by type-asserting request.GetArguments(). It skips OptionalPaginationParams, so it gets no defaults and no type errors, unlike the other list tools.
kept.fix: Call pagination, err := OptionalPaginationParams(request), return a tool error if err is set, and set opts.ListOptions = github.ListOptions{Page: pagination.Page, PerPage: pagination.PerPage}.
kept.why: ListIssues type-asserts request.GetArguments()["page"/"perPage"].(float64) by hand instead of calling OptionalPaginationParams. It repeats the shared reader, but without its defaults or type errors.

kept.problem: The tail_lines default of 500 is written twice: in mcp.DefaultNumber(500) at line 562 and in the hand-written `if tailLines == 0 { tailLines = 500 }`.
kept.fix: Add a const defaultTailLines = 500, use it in mcp.DefaultNumber, and read the value with OptionalIntParamWithDefault(request, "tail_lines", defaultTailLines) instead of the manual zero check.
kept.why: 500 appears both in mcp.DefaultNumber(500) and in the manual `if tailLines == 0 { tailLines = 500 }`. OptionalIntParamWithDefault together with one constant would replace both.

kept.why: actions.go:652 drops the error with `r, _ := json.Marshal(result)`. Every other json.Marshal in the file (lines 75, 214, 313, 683, 698, …) checks it. This is inconsistent error handling.

kept.why: TotalCount and IncompleteResults are already set from GetTotal()/GetIncompleteResults(). The two `if result.X != nil` blocks then set the same fields again from the same pointers, which has no effect.
